title: With Connelly Early to the IL, Sandoval, Bello in play for Red Sox rotation spot
content:
BOSTON — Somewhat overshadowed in the midst of Tuesday’s benches-clearing incident with the Washington Nationals was Boston Red Sox starter Connelly Early exiting in the fourth inning with an elbow injury. One day later, the Red Sox placed Early, one of their top young starters, on the injured list with left elbow inflammation.

The 24-year-old was set for an MRI on Wednesday morning, and the Red Sox are hopeful they will have more clarity on the severity of the injury after Wednesday afternoon’s game. Regardless, with team days off on Thursday and Monday and the All-Star break looming, interim manager Chad Tracy said it didn’t make sense to push Early, even if the injury is not severe.

“He’s feeling better today but it’s still a little sore, so with one more start remaining prior to the All-Star break — it’s not just the start, it’s like, are we going to have this guy go out in two days and throw a side session?” Tracy explained. “That’s an easy decision to make sure you take that out of his hands and do right by him.”

The Red Sox’s scheduled starters for their weekend series against the Los Angeles Angels in Anaheim are Jake Bennett, Sonny Gray and Ranger Suárez. The club then heads to Chicago to face the White Sox for a series beginning Tuesday before a three-game series against the New York Mets leading into the break. Given the days off, the next time the Red Sox will need a fifth starter is July 11.

Tracy named two potential options for that start: Patrick Sandoval and Brayan Bello.

Sandoval, who signed a two-year, $18.25 million deal with the Red Sox before the 2025 season, has not pitched in a major-league game since having an internal brace procedure on his elbow in 2024 while with the Angels. The hope when he signed was that he would return by the end of the 2025 season, but setbacks pushed back his timeline.

The left-hander finally began a rehab assignment last month and is nearing the end of the 30-day rehab window allowed for players on the IL before they need to be activated. Sandoval is expected to make one more rehab start this weekend with Double-A Portland, when he’s scheduled to throw roughly 70 pitches. That will allow him to be stretched out enough to make a start should the Red Sox call on him. Sandoval does not have minor-league options, so he would have to be activated, traded or released once his rehab clock ends.

“We’ll see how he feels coming out of (the Saturday start) and then make our decision,” Tracy said.

The other option is Bello, the much-maligned right-hander who had been a Red Sox rotation mainstay the past three-plus seasons before he was optioned to Triple A in June after a brutal start to the season.

In three Triple-A starts entering Wednesday, Bello has a 3.95 ERA with 16 strikeouts and four walks in 13 2/3 innings. Bello is set to start on Wednesday for Worcester.

Tracy said the Red Sox want Bello to continue attacking with his off-speed stuff. While Bello remains an option, Tracy seemed to indicate the preference would be for the right-hander to keep working in Worcester.

“It’s not like ‘Oh, he’s not going to be here again’; there’s all kinds of things you can do with the rotation leading into the break,” Tracy said. “So we’re still talking about Brayan, but right now he’s taking on that (Triple-A) start today which is we’re making progress there.”

Meanwhile, in an effort to bolster their infield depth following a slew of injuries over the past month, the Red Sox made a trade Wednesday morning, acquiring infielder Brett Harris from the Athletics for minor-league right-hander Ben Hansen. They optioned Harris to Triple A. To make room on the 40-man roster, the Red Sox DFA’d reliever Tommy Kahnle, who allowed four runs in one inning Tuesday night.

In 37 Triple-A games this season, Harris has hit .336 with a .978 OPS and has played first, second and third base.

“We’ve gotten fairly thin on infield depth over the course of the last couple of weeks, so with a roster spot opening up to get him over here is helpful,” Tracy said.

The Red Sox also activated reliever Jovani Moran from the IL and recalled reliever Alec Gamboa on Wednesday to bolster their bullpen with Kahnle gone and Early on the IL.
